subjects.displayTitle: Station of the Manifestation of God: revelation, recognition and response
subjects.introduction: How can the unknowable God be known through a human life? ‘Abdu’l-Bahá begins the answer with what a divine educator does: hearts are transformed, a humiliated people is raised to glory, the springtime of the soul returns, and no school could have supplied the knowledge that did it. Then the question deepens. The Manifestation is a mirror that reveals the sun without containing it, a Word whose meaning exceeds the voice that speaks it, a servant who prays and fasts and is driven into exile, and at the same time the one through whom creation was called into being. Holding those claims together without collapsing them is the real work: noticing who is speaking, which station is being described, and why unity of purpose among the Messengers does not erase their distinct missions. John’s account of the Word made flesh [1] and the Qur’an’s pairing of divine incomparability with a single religious summons [2] sharpen the inquiry from outside. The path leads on into the sun and the mirror as images, into the Primal Will and preexistence, into the Manifestation’s relationship to God, and finally back to daily life, where recognition shows itself as justice, trustworthiness and care for the poor.

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: The holy divine Manifestations are all heavenly Artists. Upon the canvas of creation with the brush of their deeds and [lives] and actions, they paint immortal pictures which cannot be found in any Art Museum of Europe and America but you find these masterpieces of these spiritual Artists in the hearts.

order.why: Open with the recorded challenge about placing Baha’u’llah beside earlier educators and the reply asking readers to examine His teachings.
shortened: Rev. Bixby: By what authority is Baha'u'llah placed with Abraham, Moses and Jesus?

A. B: Today we believe Baha'u'llah to be an educator of humanity, as Abraham, Moses and Jesus were educators. Are His teachings worthy of serious attention? He originated and proclaimed them. He caused others to believe and follow them. What is the function of a teacher and educator of humanity? By what evidence shall we recognize him? Is it not his power to train and develop, as children are trained at school?

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: Even Christ did not become manifest that we should merely believe in Him as the Christ, follow Him and adore His mention.

Nay, rather, Christ appeared in order to illumine the world of humanity, to render the earthly world celestial, to make the human kingdom a realm of angels, to unite the hearts, to enkindle the light of love in human souls, so that such souls might become independent, attaining complete unity and fellowship, turning to God, entering into the divine Kingdom, receiving the bounties and bestowals of God and partaking of the manna from heaven.

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: For example, Christ was capable of leading spirits into that abode of serenity. He was capable of guiding hearts into that haven of rest. From the day of His manifestation to the present time He has been resuscitating hearts and quickening spirits. He has exercised that vivifying influence in the realm of hearts and spirits; therefore, His resuscitating is everlasting.

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: The real Manifestation of God must be endowed with divine knowledge and not dependent upon learning acquired in schools. He must be the Educator, not the educated; His standard, intuition instead of tuition. He must be perfect and not imperfect, great and glorious instead of being weak and impotent. He must be wealthy in the riches of the spiritual world and not indigent.

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: In the human world, there have appeared souls who became educators of humanity, who shone like the sun and were worshipped throughout all regions - they were the dawning-places of revelation and the daysprings of the light of truth. Therefore, consider in the human temple what loftiness and exaltation this represents.

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: For in this great accomplishment He stood single and alone. Could He have made such a change and brought about such a condition among these people without the sanction and assistance of a heavenly power? Could He have transformed a people from humiliation to glory without a holy and divine support?

None other than a divine power could have done this. Therein lies the proof of Prophethood because the mission of a Prophet is education of the human race such as this Personage accomplished, proving Him to be a mighty Prophet among the Prophets and His Book the very Book of God.

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: Christ was heavenly, divine and belonged to the world of the Kingdom. He was the embodiment of spiritual knowledge. His intellect was superior to these philosophers, His comprehension deeper, His perception keener, His knowledge more perfect.

order.why: Begin with a question and the transformation of human hearts; consider education and its fruits before declarations of rank.
shortened: But Prophets demonstrate the existence of this Inner Perception and Intuition in man in a practical way. They show forth this power first in themselves by inspiring men with the faculty of comprehending the realities of things and grasping things supernatural.

shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha answered in words to the following effect: "Whatever good deeds man performs in this world have been originally inculcated by the Prophets and Manifestations of God. Were it not for the Prophets' teachings, man would remain ignorant and heedless like unto the brute beasts.
Hence true excellence consists in acknowledging the Manifestations of God and loving up to their teachings. (For they set the standard of a truly good life and enable men to perform Good Deeds.)"

shortened: The centers of progress for each age are the manifestations of God as seen in his prophets. In whatever country or at whatever time they appear, they are the focus of the creational day - for as the sun in the material heaven develops the material beings, so do these spiritual suns develop the world of minds and souls.

By man is meant the perfect individual, and that perfect individual is like a mirror wherein divine perfections appear and are visible. However, the Sun does not descend from its height of sanctity and enter into the mirror, but when the mirror is pure and faces the Sun of Reality, the perfections of the Sun of Reality - which are its rays and heat - become manifest and visible in that mirror. These souls are the Holy Manifestations of God.

All the perfections, bounties and splendours of the one true God are plainly visible in the realities of His Holy Manifestations, even as the light of the sun is fully reflected with all its perfections and bounties in a clear and spotless mirror.

The sun does not leave his place in the heavens and descend into the mirror, for the actions of ascent and descent, coming and going, do not belong to the Infinite, they are the methods of finite beings. In the Manifestation of God, the perfectly polished mirror, appear the qualities of the Divine in a form that man is capable of comprehending.

For He is like a pure and delicate mirror wherein are reflected sublime images that tell of the Sun of Reality which shines upon it with eternal grace.

I also considered the situation appropriate for saying, "His Holiness the Bab states, 'I am the Mirror of God.'[26] His purpose is to show the Sanctified Manifestations teach that, 'God's Effulgence shines upon Us, and from Us shines upon the creation.' It is in this station that They claim divinity. If the sun shining in the mirror claims that it is the sun, indeed it has spoken the truth."

shortened: That is, they are all Divine Manifestations and the reality of Divinity is ever sanctified above ascent, descent, incarnation and emergence. Whatever man thinks comes from his own imagination, therefore there is no incarnation, no emergence, and no ascent. Incarnation and admixture are properties of physical bodies. The utmost is that these holy Manifestations are like mirrors and the rays of the Sun of Reality are reflected in these mirrors. Therefore if that Sun which is reflected in the mirrors says "I am the Sun," it is the very truth. Despite this, It does not say It has incarnated, for that Sun is eternally in Its lofty sanctity.

shortened: The Holy Tree (Sadrat) is, in a sense, the Manifestation of the One True God, exalted be He. The Blessed Tree in the land of Za'faran refereth to the land which is flourishing, blessed, holy and all-perfumed, where that Tree hath been planted. The intent of all exalted names and titles revealed in the Bayan and from the Pen of the Most High in this Revelation is the Manifestation of God Himself.

But thou hast beheld the light of the Most Great Guidance in the blessed Mount of Certitude, the holy valley of the All-Merciful, as a kindled fire in the Blessed Tree of Man, and thou hast heard the soul-stirring call "Verily, I am God, thy Lord and the Lord of thy forefathers" from the divine throat.

The great ones are from all time in their glorious station, their reality is luminous from the beginning, the reality that causes the qualities of God to appear, but the day of their manifestation is the day when they proclaim themselves of this earth.

shortened: Having barred the way that leadeth unto Thee, Thou hast, by virtue of Thine authority and through the potency of Thy will, called into being Them Who are the Manifestations of Thy Self, and hast entrusted Them with Thy message unto Thy people, and caused Them to become the Daysprings of Thine inspiration, the Exponents of Thy Revelation, the Treasuries of Thy Knowledge and the Repositories of Thy Faith, that all men may, through Them, turn their faces towards Thee, and may draw nigh unto the kingdom of Thy Revelation and the heaven of Thy grace.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: And since the gates of knowledge and comprehension were closed, and the ultimate degree of the servants' understanding rejected, the Sovereign of existence, through His grace and bounty, caused the Manifestations of Oneness and Daysprings of Divine glory to appear from the horizon of "Verily, I am He Who is manifest above all things," so that all people might attain unto the knowledge of God through recognition of these Suns dawning from the horizon of truth, and might be blessed with obedience to God and submission to His will through obedience to these holy Beings.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: Prophets do not comprehend the God Essence. To comprehend the Sun of Reality we would have to be greater (than the Sun). In order to comprehend the Essence of God a Prophet would have to encompass the Infinite.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: None can transcend or rise beyond this exalted station - the station of recognition and attainment unto that Sun of Oneness and Daystar of Truth - for it is clearly impossible to reach the Unknowable Essence. Thus do the waves of that hidden Ocean surge in this divine Manifestation, and the rays of that invisible Sun shine forth from the horizon of this holy and eternal Dawn without any intimation.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: Immeasurably high are the Prophets of God exalted above the comprehension of men, who can never know them except by their own Selves. Far be it from His glory that His chosen Ones should be magnified by any other than their own persons. Glorified are they above the praise of men; exalted are they above human understanding!

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: He cannot be known except through Himself, nor described save by His own Self. None hath ever encompassed this hidden secret and treasured mystery, nor ever shall. Whatever hath been mentioned is but as a shadow before the lights of the Sun of Truth.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: O Ahmad! The station of the Manifestation is above what the servants mention of Him. Then shineth forth the light of unity and are extinguished the lamps of fancy and conjecture.

shortened: Thou hast asked about a station greater than the creation of the heavens and earth, which God hath placed above the testimonies of His servants - none shall understand it save them that are endued with knowledge. Yea, people understand according to their ranks and stations, not according to that which hath been ordained for it. Glorified, glorified be He above all that ye ask!

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: Know thou, moreover, that the Truth and whatsoever proceedeth from Him must needs be distinguished from creation and whatsoever emanateth therefrom. This verily is a certain truth. He can never be confused with aught else, and shineth forth from the horizon of the heaven of holiness with manifest sovereignty.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: Praise be to God, Who made His creatures to know the station of His theophany through His very Self; Who confirmed the signs of knowledge by the decree of His wisdom, without likeness or anthropomorphism; Who deposited the pattern of differentiation within the realities of hearts, without making similitude unto Himself; and Who sent down the verses of Sinai upon the forms of contingent beings, without any definition derived from aught else.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: Thou hast made them the pillars of Thy unity, the interpreters of Thy revelation, the manifestations of Thy Self, and the signs of Thy sovereignty. Thou hast removed all distinction between Thee and them in the station of guidance unto Thee, such that all behold in the station of their knowledge Thy knowledge, in the station of their love Thy love, in the station of their manifestation Thy manifestation, and in the station of their concealment the sovereignty of Thy power.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: After establishing this lofty station and this glorious seat, true oneness refers to His Vicegerent amongst His servants. He is the Dawning-Place of revelation, the Dayspring of inspiration, the Manifestation of His Self and the Repository of knowledge. He is the Treasury of names and attributes. Whoso hath known Him hath known God, and whoso hath clung unto Him hath clung unto God.

In the Dispensation of the Furqan, the Seal of the Prophets (may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for His sake) attained this station. Were any likeness or peer to be found for that Essence of existence and Cause of creation, how could the sanctification of the Creator's Being from peers and likeness be established?

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: The Person of the Manifestation hath ever been the representative and mouthpiece of God. He, in truth, is the Dayspring of God’s most excellent Titles, and the Dawning-Place of His exalted Attributes.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: These gates, which in truth are primarily the gates of the effusions of the King of Oneness, are the guides of the Way and the bearers of proof and evidence. They are the Manifestations of Names and Attributes, and the Dawning-places of revelation and signs. In every age and cycle, a gate among the gates was opened to the face of creation through a name among the Names, until it culminated in the ultimate gates of the Most Great Grace, the Most Noble Station, the Supreme Rank, and the Uttermost Goal.

order.why: Move from the limits of knowledge toward mediation, attributes and the Primal Will; retain the distinction between the divine Essence and its signs.
shortened: As for the heavenly spirit, it is a holy essence, a perfect word, a complete sign, the mystery of existence, and the reality hidden from the eyes of all beings. It is the Supreme Pen, the Most Merciful Soul, and the manifestation of Truth from the dawning-place of creation and its sun at the point of invention. This is specifically for the Prophets in the worlds of creation.

shortened: Then, through the requirements of the establishment of the Sovereign of justice upon the throne of mercy and grace, He created, through pure origination and sheer invention, the Point of existence and the Praiseworthy Countenance, which has been expressed through various terms such as the Eternal Countenance, the Divine Reed, the Primal Point, the Warbling of the Dove, the Perfect Word of Manifestation, the Divine Identity of the Cloud of Unknowing, and the Countenance of Ahmad and Muhammad.

Then did His Glory shine forth in its own essence, and He cast into its identity the image of His Self. Thus was manifested from it that which was within and upon it, filling thereby the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them.

Verily He is the gatherer of all ranks and exalted stations, heavenly realities, celestial subtleties, and divine outpourings. Likewise He is the gatherer of created realities and contingent darkness. In truth, He is the Greatest Medium, the Supreme Intermediary, the meeting place of the two seas, the confluence of the two rivers, and the possessor of two stations.

shortened: Know that, while the Manifestations of God possess infinite virtues and perfections, They occupy only three stations: The first is the material station; the second is the human station, which is that of the rational soul; and the third is that of divine manifestation and heavenly splendour.

order.why: Hold material life, distinctive spiritual station, servitude and divine speech together without rewriting their different voices or qualifications.
shortened: Even the holy, divine Manifestations have had a nature in the utmost equilibrium, the health and wholesomeness of their bodies most perfect, their constitutions endowed with physical vigor, their powers functioning in perfect order, and the outward sensations linked with the inward perceptions, working together with extraordinary momentum and coordination.

order.why: Hold material life, distinctive spiritual station, servitude and divine speech together without rewriting their different voices or qualifications.
shortened: Although those Manifestations are outwardly raised up in human form, in reality they are holy essences and sanctified realities.

shortened: The divine Holy Prophets have two stations. The first is the station of "Abstraction." This is the station wherein they commune with God, receive the Graces of the Holy Spirit and become intimate with the Fragrances of Holiness. The second station is the station of "Plurality." In this station they occupy themselves with the education of mankind.

order.why: Hold material life, distinctive spiritual station, servitude and divine speech together without rewriting their different voices or qualifications.

His utterance is but revealed revelation."

order.why: Hold material life, distinctive spiritual station, servitude and divine speech together without rewriting their different voices or qualifications.
shortened: The Holy Manifestations have two stations: one station specific to them which none other may follow, and a station which all must follow. The second station comprises God's law and teachings. They are like a physician - for a physician in perfect health may do things that patients must not follow. Likewise, whatever the Holy Manifestations choose, whatever they do, whatever they enact contains perfect wisdom.

When we say "The Apostle believed in what was revealed to him," his belief is not like the belief of others. When we say that Moses and his companion forgot their fish, their forgetfulness is not like that of others. This is the station where it is said "The good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those drawn nigh."

questions: The opening asks what makes a divine educator and then turns to the transformation of hearts. How do the later passages on revelation, innate knowledge and authority deepen or challenge an account based only on observable effects?

What does each image—sun, mirror, tree, Word or Book—make possible to understand, and where does it cease to help? How do the explicit limits placed on analogy affect your reading of the most exalted declarations?

How do the passages distinguish the unknowable divine Essence, the Manifestation and other human beings? What can the different accounts of material life, servitude and divine speech illuminate when read together without erasing their distinctions?

Where do the readings affirm unity, and where do they insist on distinct missions or stations? How do the speaker, recipient, historical occasion, translation status and difference between written text and reported conversation shape what a passage can support?

Compare John 1:1–18 and Qur’an 42:11–13 with the collection. What different ways of speaking about transcendence, revelation and the knowledge of God emerge? Which similarities invite further inquiry, and which differences should remain unresolved by a simple analogy?

The final readings connect recognition with justice, trustworthy conduct, care and freedom from racial superiority. How might studying divine station change a relationship or a practice of service? Which connected subject would help you examine that possibility more closely?

references.note: Read John 1:1–18 in the King James Version. The opening connects the Word with God, creation, life and light, then speaks of the Word becoming flesh and making the unseen God known. Compare it with this collection’s language of the Word, human and divine stations, and the mirror that reveals the sun without containing it. How does each text describe the possibility of knowing God? What changes when the image is light, a mirror or the Word made flesh? John also distinguishes the witness from the light and describes both reception and rejection. Attend to those distinctions as well as the parallels: the Christian language of Incarnation and the Baha’i rejection of divine descent into a body should remain visible in the comparison.

references.note: Read Qur’an 42:11–13, including the English rendering by Dr Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran. The passage places God’s incomparability beside hearing, seeing, providence and knowledge, then recalls the religious way enjoined upon Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad and warns against division. Compare this conjunction with the readings on the unknowable Essence, the knowledge conveyed through revelation and the unity of the Manifestations. How can a text affirm both transcendence and relationship? What kind of unity is being asked of its hearers? Preserve the Qur’anic setting: these verses invite comparison but do not themselves set out the Baha’i account of the station of a Manifestation.
